name: Purslane
short: Case report: acute kidney injury from oxalate in two elderly patients after eating large amounts. In two trials adverse events were mild to moderate and did not differ significantly from placebo.
text: A case report describes two elderly patients who developed acute kidney injury, attributed to oxalate nephropathy, after high dietary consumption of purslane; both needed haemodialysis and were discharged after their kidney function improved. In small randomised trials adverse events were mild to moderate: in a four-week trial of oral purslane syrup for hand eczema, 10 participants on purslane and 4 on placebo had adverse events (a difference that was not statistically significant), and in a 12-week trial of purslane extract in 63 adults with type 2 diabetes the few adverse events were mild and did not differ from placebo. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
